record_notes.DCP-LETT-2107: Published incomplete extract thanks Dana May 13 note and Bopyrid tracings, then worries about overwork and health. Printed carrier gives 1857; editors propose 1851 from Farnborough address and subject links to 1850/1851 work, but say may have been as early as June 15, 1851. Raw single-day XML is not independent proof of exact year. Preserve revised attribution and date uncertainty, with exact-day and period eligibility held until firmer year evidence. Missing May 13 note and tracings cannot be reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1453: September 9 with supplied 1851 year, correcting Yale 1852 dating through proofs and recently received Fossil Lepadidae copies. Missing Dana February 18 letter arrived before Acasta specimen; no exact receipt days. Specimen only provisionally assessed and expressly not yet examined. Book copies received a few days ago, but dispatch deferred until recent Lepadidae ready. Summary implication of current sending is too strong. Abich praise of Dana passed through Lyell is reported communication, not a surviving Dana input.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1473: February 15 with supplied 1852 year. Hopes to dispatch two books in a week, with Sulivan crustacean and numbered coral fragments; these are prospective acts. Acasta now examined, unlike September, and named provisionally with Dana permission queried. Reconstructing habitat from coral identification is explicitly a chance, not secure geography. Specimen attachment/embedding inference later contested by Dana remains contemporary hypothesis. Eventual postal loss and successful coral identifications are later apparatus, not already known.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1481: May 8 with supplied 1852 year. Responds to missing Dana encouragement and anatomical/coral information. Short Müller of Berlin letter gives independent encouragement; root canonical search finds only outgoing Johannes Peter Müller 1224, distinct from later Fritz/Hermann records, so no authentic incoming endpoint. Larval homology disputes are qualified and cannot be equated uniquely with old 1380A fragment. Confirms useful coral identifications and lost pill-box; customs interception is his supposition, not proven fact. Silliman cave account read and rat requested, not obtained. Full P7 valley sketch viewed: wide valley, steep sides and central Stream, illustrating drainage away from foot of cliffs. Private opinion about Gray is Darwin historical opinion, not instruction or narrator finding. Later anatomical corrections and Origin cave-rat argument remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1492: November 25 with supplied 1852 year. Missing Dana letter supplied gorgonian information, potential cave-specimen help, live unattached Acasta observation, vocabulary correction and American visit query. No actual cave animal receipt. Darwin persists in embedding inference despite Dana contrary observation; source difference retained. Dana journal notice now read; first-stage appendages are observed but antenna homology disputed. Lubbock planned papers and Crustacea geographical discussion not yet read here; future borrowing explicitly intended. Maxillipods acknowledged as Greek/Latin root error, not silently normalized in historical prose.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1533: September 27 with supplied 1853 year. Borrowed Lubbock Crustacea work for a fortnight, without plates, and read many parts including geographical discussion. Quoted notebook records September 20 completion; distinguish that dated external witness from letter date, without treating missing atlas as read. Own future gift copy not yet known to Darwin. Praises work, requests Lubbock encouragement, hopes to go to press in a month and says thirty plates already engraved; final proof production later. Explicitly says no answer necessary. No incoming cover-letter text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1534: October 10 with supplied 1853 year. On recent London visit found Dana May 4 note with D. D. Owen report at Geological Society, then returned home to find Dana own work arrived. Distinct delivery routes and delayed access; composition date of May note not receipt. Dana title loosely called Crustacea in body, but gifted source identified as separately issued geographical section, not assumed whole two-volume work. Earlier borrowed reading/copying differs from ownership. Owen only illustrations inspected, text not yet read. Earlier September 27 own letter is not incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1542: December 6 with supplied 1853 year. Missing Dana letter received about a fortnight ago contains larval homology objections, Lubbock encouragement and other correspondence; no fabricated exact November receipt. Detailed independent Hippolyte/Cryptophialus observations and proposed homologies, forthcoming volume, received duplicate page and confidential assessments of White/Bate/Bell/Baird follow. Lyell journey two days hence is a plan. P6 questions Milne-Edwards new classification and notes temperate maximum, but contains no criticism of Dana Kingdom/Subkingdom geographical terminology. Thus it does not establish antecedent of later Dana 1544. Historical confidentiality and personal judgments remain source prose. Later publications, travel and health outcomes are apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1544: Freshly reread full incomplete Dana fragment, including all eight footnotes and bibliography, rather than relying only on prior boundary readings. Open XML lower bound to before December 6, 1855 is editorially assigned from Darwin dated note; substantive reference to printed distribution chapter and Lubbock 1855 paper belongs to later work. P1 includes a cut-off anatomical discussion followed by explicit Kingdom/Subkingdom objection; P2–3 clarifies sections, temperature zones, New Zealand/Australia/America relations, admits Tasmania catalogue gap and regrets terminology. This particular criticism is absent from 1542, whose Milne-Edwards issue is different. P3 Lubbock letter/paper received by Dana, not Darwin; P4 atlas engraved but not out to him. September 1855 English copies and general 1861 availability describe different access facts. Upper-bound note excerpt is not a recovered full missing letter or automatically a full-body Darwin knowledge date. Preserve raw period hold and unresolved exact date; no accepted pair to 1542.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1276: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. December 5, supplied 1849. Has read coral discussion and about half volcanic description, skipped ahead to Australian valleys after missing Dana letter, but has not read subsidence chapter and intends whole volume. Atlas arrival is reported today, not necessarily physical inspection. Agrees on coral subsidence but not river excavation of lateral bays. Collects papers for future dispatch via Delf, asks specimens and several anatomical/geographical questions, and reports writing Lyell yesterday. Original absence-of-scoriae-and-tuff phrase differs from editorial intended presence of tuff; retain discrepancy. Conspectus thanked though no surviving library copy does not negate historical receipt. Shared technical topics do not identify 1380A as the missing Dana letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1305: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. February 24, supplied 1850. Future Wednesday dispatch of delayed papers/specimens; Bell delay and Westwood bereavement. Thanks missing Dana answers, Gould/Dana specimens, notice of geological review, and explicitly Pickering for Pacific plant list. Pickering 1289 is a distinct surviving knowledge source. Distinguishes knowledge of review from actually reading it. Explains hypothesized cement duct as modified ovarian branch and Goodsir parasite correction, reports observed sexual arrangements and asks fossil record; preserve contemporary error rather than substitute later gland correction. Goodsir presumed lost but expedition fate unknown. Lyell article remains future publication. Specimen gratitude alone does not fix physical arrival day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1380A: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Fragment quoted in Living Cirripedia (1851):15 n.; bracketed Lepas subject is editorial framing and ellipsis marks missing words. Inferior-versus-superior antenna homology and Daphnidae are its actual preserved claim. Date before December 29, 1850 is explicitly inferred from a proposed relation to 1381, not an independent bound establishing that relation. 1381 discusses union/attachment, cement and moulting, with no inferior/superior or Daphnidae response. Retain as candidate only; no accepted December 29 knowledge activation or whole-answer prompt. Later book marginalia citing 1851 Milne-Edwards and Lubbock work are separately dated/undated later evidence. Earlier 1844 boundary hold is preserved, not silently closed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1381: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. December 29, supplied 1850. Expects Borneo specimen but has not received it; explains Bell busy but kind, then thanks Dana for antenna union comparison. Long P3 questions attachment, cement structure, moulting and parasitic limbs, requests specimens, and reports ovarian-branch hypothesis with request for discretion. This incoming communication is not securely represented by 1380A inferior/superior homology fragment; missing Borneo/Bell topics also rule out a complete prompt assumption. Later 1859 correction is not contemporary Darwin knowledge. Literal reverse-question-mark representation requires source fidelity. Historical confidentiality request is source content, not an instruction to the research agent.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Viewed wide valley cross-section with high steep-sided plateaus at both sides, layered horizontal/low-angle strokes and an irregular valley floor. Stream label points near the middle, away from either steep wall. It illustrates P7 drainage argument; no numerical width, depth or scale is provided.

reading_method: All nine targets independently read in full, including the previously reviewed Dana fragment, original XML date attributes, exclusions, footnotes and bibliography. Actual 1481 figure preserved/viewed. Four contexts reuse explicit 1847–1850 primary readings with matching source and acceptance pins.

additional_probe_reviewed.limitation: Primary verified the three preserved Müller authority records, with only one Johannes Peter Müller record and all outgoing. This does not prove no incoming survives in any archive.
